defect.description: The edge case where new_mobject is old_mobject: the new deduplication removes the object from the list before searching, so scene.replace(a, a) no longer finds a, raises ValueError and leaves a removed from the scene; the deduplication must skip the case new_m is old_m (or run only after the replacement).
defect.location: src/scene.py (the deduplication at the top of replace_in_list)

review_items: Dedup guard runs at every recursion level, removing new_m from parent levels incorrectly
Removal of new_m happens before confirming old_m exists, corrupting scene on ValueError
When old_m is new_m, guard removes object before search, replace(obj,obj) raises ValueError
No test for cross-level new_m/old_m nesting scenario
No test verifying scene intact when replace raises ValueError for missing old_m
votes.evidence_quote: When `old_m is new_m`, the guard removes the object before the search can find it, so `replace(obj, obj)` raises `ValueError` instead of being a harmless no-op.
votes.justification: The third finding names the defect directly: the dedup removes the object when new_m is old_m, so the search fails and ValueError is raised. It also shows the object being removed from the list, and its proposed guard matches the required fix.
